raw: {"analysis":"Response CCF correctly identifies that schema locks are irreversible without a full restore and explicitly requires a pre-deployment snapshot verification, whereas QXV vaguely mentions a rollback script and dry-run. QXV provides more concrete error message specifications and HTTP status codes, but introduces a canary deployment strategy that conflicts with the requirement for immediate implementation and the isolated nature of the data-pipeline cluster. Response CCF better addresses the timeline constraint by specifying local testing must conclude by Thursday EOD to accommodate the 45-minute CI run and dual-approval process before the Friday deadline.","verdict":"CCF"}
